To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) UD is the ideal framework for the representation of user generated content, (ii) the UD guidelines are flexible enough to accommodate the annotation of such texts, (iii) the annotation of user generated content in UD is a challenging task, (iv) there are several treebanks of user generated content already available in UD, (v) there is a need for the development of guidelines for the annotation of user-generated content, (vi) we provide a set of tentative guidelines for this purpose

UD is a suitable framework for treebanking user generated content, as it provides a consistent set of annotation guidelines, which can be used to annotate the particular phenomena of user generated content, such as the ones presented in this paper, and thus promote consistency across treebanks.

UD is a suitable framework for the annotation of UGC, that the annotation criteria of existing treebanks are not consistent, and that a set of tentative annotation guidelines is proposed to address the issue.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of annotation guidelines for the UD framework, which are intended for use in the annotation of UD treebanks of user generated content, in order to promote consistent annotation of the linguistic phenomena found in such texts across languages.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UD is not yet a complete solution to the annotation of user generated content, but the guidelines presented here can be a good starting point for future work.

the UD framework has proven to be an excellent choice for the annotation of user-generated content, since it allows for the representation of the linguistic phenomena of these texts in a very natural and straightforward way.
the UD framework is the best choice for the development of treebanks featuring social media and user generated content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this paper provides a set of annotation principles and guidelines for UD treebanks that contain user generated content, which is a growing phenomenon, and which has been treated in an inconsistent way so far.
this paper is the first attempt to unify the annotation of user generated text within UD.
we propose a unified representation of user generated content in UD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UD framework is well suited to capture most of the phenomena found in user generated content, but that some phenomena are not covered in the current UD guidelines.
, despite the fact that UD has already been applied in the annotation of user-generated content, there is a lack of a unified approach for the treatment of such data.
UD can be used for the annotation of user generated texts, as well as for the annotation of the main phenomena that are found in them.
